dedupe_keys.name: data and code for china s crowdsourced data reveal pathways to enhance urban flood resilience

description: A Zhejiang University research team publishes a Chinese national urban-flooding inventory and rainfall-threshold results. Zenodo provides a data-and-code archive under CC BY 4.0. The description identifies historical waterlogging and flooding events for districts and counties from 2010 to 2021, spatial shapefiles, statistical CSVs, figure scripts and hourly-rainfall threshold lines derived from an Ensemble SSVM-ANF model. These materials can calibrate urban flood occurrence and warning-threshold components of water and transport simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this versioned inventory. Coverage is China’s administrative units and the crowdsourced event evidence used by the study, not every inundated street. A limitation is that reported events may reflect uneven public attention and district-level locations cannot identify asset-level depth. The threshold model inherits its training and rainfall-record assumptions. No archive was downloaded or event count and threshold performance independently checked.
